title: Adjuvant abemaciclib + endocrine therapy

agents.name: Abemaciclib
agents.explanation: Abemaciclib inhibits CDK4 and CDK6 proteins. These proteins help cells move towards division. It is combined with endocrine treatment to reduce recurrence risk in eligible high-risk early breast cancer.
agents.watch: Start the prescribed diarrhoea rescue plan at the first loose stool and contact the team. Breathlessness, a swollen painful leg, fever or jaundice need prompt assessment.

agents.name: Your endocrine treatment
agents.explanation: The chosen endocrine medicine either reduces oestrogen production or blocks its action. An aromatase inhibitor may need ovarian suppression before menopause. The exact drug and duration are prescribed separately.
agents.watch: Tell the team about joint pain, hot flushes, vaginal symptoms and mood changes. The bone-health and clot-risk discussion depends on the drug chosen.
risks: Hot flushes, joint or muscle symptoms
Bone loss with AI / ovarian suppression
Clot and uterine risks with tamoxifen

context_label: HR-positive / HER2-negative early breast cancer · adjuvant
purpose: For eligible high-risk node-positive early breast cancer, adding abemaciclib to endocrine therapy reduces the risk of recurrence after surgery.
schedule_summary: Abemaciclib is taken twice daily continuously, with endocrine treatment, for up to two years if appropriate. A 28-day block is shown for orientation; there is no planned tablet-free week. Endocrine treatment usually continues longer.

phases_note: A general pathway, not an appointment calendar. Your team confirms the order, overlap and duration; no date entry is needed.
timeline_note: Treatment bands show the source schedule. Symptom bands show possible patterns, not measured probabilities; serious effects can occur at any time.
safety_note: Fever, shivers or suddenly feeling unwell require immediate contact. Serious symptoms override the timeline or diary.
teachback: Can you explain the current phase, which checks are expected next, and which symptoms mean you should call today? You do not need to enter dates to read the plan.
consent_support: Discuss the treatment aim, alternatives, expected benefit, serious and lasting risks, fertility/pregnancy precautions, the planned monitoring and who to contact. Review the full longitudinal pathway and confirm which conditional treatments apply.
urgent_extra: Report new breathlessness, chest symptoms, severe diarrhoea, inability to drink, jaundice, a painful swollen leg or a severe rash promptly. You do not need to identify which medicine caused the symptom.

support.title: Diarrhoea plan
support.text: Have the prescribed antidiarrhoeal medicine available. Start the agreed plan at the first loose stool and call early.

support.title: Daily tablets
support.text: Take the prescribed dose at regular times. Do not double up after a missed or vomited dose.

support.title: Baseline and ongoing checks
support.text: Baseline FBC, renal, liver and bone profile. Baseline ECG as clinically indicated. Bloods every two weeks for two months, then monthly for two months, then as indicated. No routine ribociclib-style Day 14 ECG schedule.

support.title: Endocrine and bone care
support.text: Confirm endocrine/OFS treatment, bone-health assessment and the longer-term follow-up plan.

questions.q: How does this fit around surgery and radiotherapy?
questions.a: Abemaciclib is taken with endocrine treatment after surgery and other indicated local/systemic treatment. Abemaciclib is planned for two years; endocrine treatment commonly continues beyond that.

questions.q: Do I need to enter dates?
questions.a: No. Both charts explain the expected sequence and general intervals without any dates or personal information. Your hospital arranges actual appointments.
The treatment journey lists baseline and ongoing checks, why they matter and what to ask. It does not mark tests as booked or completed.

questions.q: What happens if treatment is delayed?
questions.a: Your team may delay, reduce, change or stop a medicine. Ask which component changes and what happens to the next review; do not restart independently.

questions.q: What about fertility, pregnancy or breastfeeding?
questions.a: Discuss fertility preservation and reproductive plans before treatment. The team should explain contraception and breastfeeding restrictions for every medicine, including how long precautions continue afterwards.

questions.q: How should I use trial numbers?
questions.a: Trial results describe groups with defined eligibility. Ask how well those patients and their treatment match your situation; the figures are not an individual prediction.

questions.q: Which checks are baseline, and which happen during treatment?
questions.a: NCCP 00619 specifies baseline ECG as clinically indicated. It does not mandate the ribociclib Cycle 1 Day 14 ECG schedule. Abemaciclib is continuous twice daily: there is no routine seven-day break.

evidence.title: monarchE: seven-year invasive disease-free survival
evidence.intro: The treatment setting, trial population and endpoint matter when interpreting benefit.
evidence.population: A phase III trial of high-risk, node-positive HR-positive/HER2-negative early breast cancer compared two years of abemaciclib plus endocrine therapy with endocrine therapy alone.

metrics.label: Estimated invasive disease-free survival at 7 years

evidence.interpretation: Seven-year invasive disease-free survival was 77.4% versus 70.9% (6.5 percentage points difference). This composite endpoint is not the same as overall survival and does not predict an individual outcome. The 2025 primary overall-survival report also found an overall-survival benefit. Treatment eligibility still requires the NCCP high-risk and timing criteria.

items.title: The larger pathway
items.text: Abemaciclib is taken with endocrine treatment after surgery and other indicated local/systemic treatment. Abemaciclib is planned for two years; endocrine treatment commonly continues beyond that.

items.title: Early blood monitoring
items.text: Baseline; every 2 weeks for 2 months; monthly for the next 2 months. Checks blood counts and kidney/liver/bone-profile results. Confirm blood-test appointments even though the medicine is taken at home.

items.title: Early diarrhoea support
items.text: From the first loose stool and throughout treatment. Diarrhoea can develop early and cause dehydration. Use the prescribed rescue plan and contact the team; do not wait for the next review.

items.title: Know the continuing plan
items.text: The CDK4/6 drug ends while endocrine treatment may continue. Ask for the continuing endocrine, bone-health and follow-up plan.

items.title: Keep reporting symptoms
items.text: New or lasting symptoms need assessment between appointments and after treatment stops. Ask for a written summary of continuing medicines, follow-up tests and the contact plan.

steps.title: Before starting
steps.text: Confirm the exact tablet strength, endocrine partner, blood-test and ECG plan where relevant.

steps.title: At home
steps.text: Take tablets whole at the prescribed times. Abemaciclib is continuous twice daily; ribociclib has a planned 7-day break. Follow the schedule for this card only.

steps.title: If a dose is missed or vomited
steps.text: Do not double up or take a replacement dose. Follow the medicine instructions and ask the oncology pharmacist if uncertain.

steps.title: Before the next supply
steps.text: Confirm symptoms and required test results have been reviewed. Ask whether the prescription changes; do not restart a held medicine yourself.

details.title: Interactions and storage
details.text: Check all new medicines and supplements with oncology/pharmacy, avoid grapefruit, store as labelled and keep away from children. Return unwanted tablets to the pharmacy.

details.title: Endocrine and ovarian-suppression visits
details.text: An aromatase inhibitor is generally a daily tablet. Fulvestrant, when selected for metastatic treatment, has loading injections on Days 1, 15 and 29 then monthly. Ovarian-suppression injections have their own prescription and visit schedule.

details.title: No infusion pump
details.text: The CDK4/6 medicine is taken orally. An implanted port or infusion pump is not required for these tablets; other treatment may have separate access needs.

anatomy: Often starts early. Begin your prescribed diarrhoea plan and contact the team; persistent symptoms may require a treatment hold.
Keep blood tests. Fever, shivers or sudden illness: contact oncology immediately.
Keep liver blood tests. Report jaundice, dark urine or upper-abdominal discomfort promptly.
New cough or breathlessness needs prompt assessment.
A painful swollen leg or new chest / breathing symptoms needs urgent assessment. Severe breathlessness or chest pain: emergency help.
